fields.scope: Q3: the exclusive managed units are exactly the entries declared in config/managed-config-schema.yaml#global_workflow (owned_asset_roots -> <HERMES_HOME>/skills/**, owned_binary_paths -> <HERMES_HOME>/bin/**, owned_file_mappings -> SOUL.md) plus .env.template. WORK-LAB owns these units and publishes them only through integrations/executors/hermes/sync_hermes_workflow_assets.py. Nothing else under the Hermes home is managed.

Q3: content that a NATIVE component (Hermes skill curator) writes into a managed unit is not owned by WORK-LAB and is OBSERVE. The portable sync must refuse to overwrite it: no automatic deletion and no automatic promotion. A three-way comparison (last published baseline x current live x candidate) decides, and any live state the tool did not itself publish is refused. DECIDED POLICY (2026-09-17, operator ruling 'C'): curator output is preserved by FOLDING IT BACK into the repository, which stays the single authority, and live is then republished from that authority until the two match again. Folding is automatable only as ADDITIONS: `integrations/executors/hermes/curator_foldback.py` auto-accepts files added in live, lines appended to existing files, and line-ending-only differences (normalised to LF per .gitattributes), while any file removed in live, any deleted line, or any rewritten line is reported as NEEDS_REVIEW instead of being applied. The tool never writes to Hermes Home; the adopt-baseline step plus the sanctioned sync perform the live-side convergence. Rationale: the sync's whole-tree replacement semantics and the curator's in-place writes share one directory, so one of the two must be the authority; keeping the repository authoritative preserves both the curator's knowledge and the refusal behaviour that protects unknown live content.

Q3: conflicts are resolved by an operator, never by the tool. On MANAGED_ASSET_LIVE_CHANGE_REFUSED the operator inspects the target and then either (a) re-runs with --adopt-live-baseline to accept the current live content as the new baseline, (b) re-runs with --suspend <target> to stop publishing that unit while the native writer is active, or (c) first promotes the reviewed content into the repository and publishes. Publishing any of these is recorded in HERMES_HOME/.workflow-assistance-baseline.json.
